results.summary: This design implements two NAND gates using Wokwi, with the first gate taking inputs from pins 0 and 1, the second from pins 2 and 3, and their outputs combined to drive output pin 1. The documentation incorrectly states that pins 1-7 should be set high for testing. The project appears to be a beginner-level logic gate experiment.
This design uses three AND gates in a Wokwi simulation, with outputs driving pins 1-3.
The project documentation states that the design does nothing and does not work.

This design implements a reconfigurable digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) that can operate as a ring oscillator or a clock divider. By using combination between s0(in1), s1(in2) , s2(in3) below we can different division at out1. clk (in4) - clock input, input the clock signal to this pin if the chip is to be used as a clock divider, out1 is the output of the clock divider.

This design implements a shift register with a UART interface, allowing serial data to be shifted in and out. The shift register is built using flip-flops and can be used for serial-to-parallel conversion. The UART interface enables communication with external devices.
This design is a comparator circuit built in Wokwi, but the documentation is insufficient to fully describe its functionality. The project appears to be incomplete or a placeholder.

This design implements a phase detector and PLL circuit using analog components in Wokwi. The phase detector compares the phase of two input signals and generates an error signal. The PLL uses this error signal to lock onto the input frequency.
This design is a multiplexer built in Wokwi, but the documentation is insufficient to fully describe its functionality. The project appears to be incomplete or a placeholder.
This design is a 2-bit adder that takes two single-bit inputs (in0 and in1), treating each as 0 or 1, and displays their sum as a decimal integer on a 7-segment display.
This design is an 8-bit clocked display that uses flip-flops to latch input values and drive output pins. The design demonstrates sequential logic with flip-flops.
